25+ Pieces of Writing Software You Should Know About

With writing software being so expensive, it's a lot more convenient to use a combination of free programs and real life variants. For example, I found that yWriter, writemonkey, and a pinboard IRL can easily replace Scrivener. As for two other programs I used:

I use Google Docs religiously. That program is god-tier -- collaboration with reviewers becomes ridiculously easy.

AbiWord is a fine program. It can act as a nice alternative to OpenOffice's tendency to absolutely screw over all formatting in downloaded documents.

I'm with you on that one; I, myself, use a combination of OpenOffice, Vym, Treesheets and a custom version control system that I wrote for this specific purpose. I've tried replacing OpenOffice with one of those minimalist "distraction-free writing environments" but each and every one of them has either lacked something that another had or simply wasn't feature-complete.

My only gripe with OpenOffice thus far is this; the lack of markdown support. It'd be a godsend if I could just simply hit the appropriate combination of keys without having to resort to the mouse or modifier.

Have you tried LibreOffice?

I use Linux, but Office 2007 in Wine is still better than the open source alternatives as far as my needs go for word processors (which means compatibility above all). Otherwise, Google Docs is great for collaborating and Gummi is a nice, relatively clutter-free solution for LaTeX (and also available on Windows).

EDIT: Kingsoft Office is also a good alternative to MS Office, because it has the same UI, Its compatibility with .docx is also the best you'll get without using MS Office. Link: http://www.kingsoftstore.com/writer-free.html
LibreOffice <-> OpenOffice, I often get the damn program names mixed up.

First, Scrivener is not Mac OS only.

Second, I cannot recommend WriteMonkey enough. Minimalistic in terms of interface, you still have a lot of flexibility. There's a ton of customization there, so you can make your environment look however you wish. It fully supports markdown. I especially like the export options...basically you can create your own stylesheet which is then used to export your stuff to Word or HTML. It's free but accepts donations, and if you donate you get access to plugins (written in Javascript). It's really quite good, and I do almost all my writing in it.

Is this like a new state of matter like gas, liquid, solid, plasma, and Bose-Einstein condensate (not sure if that's one)...?

The classical ones are gas, liquid, solid and plasma according to wiki. This makes sense because they do not rely on any quantum effects, so are understood within classical physics. Plasma is essentially a gas that has free ions floating so it has a lot of electromagnetic effects and can conduct.

The Bose-Einstein is special because it is essentially when lots of quanta inhabit the same, lowest energy quantum state. Since so many are together, quantum effects become very noticeable as their effects, which would normally be limited to few quanta, add up.
